interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including the preoperative PSA of 6 ng/mL and the pathological T-stage of pT3a with extraprostatic extension. Positive findings include the presence of perineural invasion noted on biopsy. Countervailing points are that surgical margins were negative, seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The absence of nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding nodal status. Biopsy findings (Gleason 3+4) align with the prostatectomy specimen grade (ISUP group 2). Prognostic revision would be significantly aided by postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory. The fixed estimated horizon is 76.69 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 46.02–107.37 months; its coverage has not been validated.
